sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片当DJ的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带上300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成了一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，陈列着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: The New York City Department of Education says in 2019 only 53% of third grade students were proficient in reading.
sentences.zh: 纽约市教育局表示，2019年只有53%的三年级学生达到了阅读水平要求。

sentences.en: That rate fell to 49% in 2022.
sentences.zh: 这一比例在2022年下降到了49%。

sentences.en: That is why the city says it announced plans today to dramatically change the way children are taught to read.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么该市今天宣布计划，要彻底改变儿童阅读教学方式的原因。

sentences.en: A few weeks ago, the nation's largest public school system, New York City, abandoned its current system for teaching kids how to read.
sentences.zh: 几周前，全美最大的公立学校系统——纽约市，放弃了其现行的儿童阅读教学体系。

sentences.en: This is not just in New York.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅发生在纽约。

sentences.en: This is all across the nation.
sentences.zh: 这是全国范围内的现象。

sentences.en: 80% of the kids in Chicago do not read on grade level.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥有80%的孩子阅读能力未达年级水平。

sentences.en: In Detroit, 91% do not read on grade level.
sentences.zh: 在底特律，这一比例高达91%。

sentences.en: It was the latest and biggest acknowledgement to date that a generation of American students has been given the wrong tools to achieve literacy.
sentences.zh: 这是迄今为止最重大的一次承认，即整整一代美国学生被提供了错误的识字工具。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Dana Goldstein on the influential educator who helped create those flawed tools and is now trying to fix the problems that they created.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事达娜·戈尔茨坦将带我们了解那位参与创造了这些缺陷工具，如今又试图修复其所造成问题的教育界重量级人物。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, June 6th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月6日，星期二。

sentences.en: Dana?
sentences.zh: 达娜？

sentences.en: Good morning, Michael.
sentences.zh: 早上好，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: I can see that you've brought some books and I think we're going to need them.
sentences.zh: 我看到你带了一些书，我想我们待会儿会用到它们。

sentences.en: So, thank you for doing that.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你这么做。

sentences.en: We're here to talk about how kids learn to read in the United States.
sentences.zh: 我们今天来聊聊美国的孩子们是如何学习阅读的。

sentences.en: And so, to begin with,
sentences.zh: 那么，首先，

sentences.en: I think it would be useful for you to define and demonstrate the big schools of thought that exist in American education about the best way to teach kids to read.
sentences.zh: 我想请你定义并演示一下美国教育界关于儿童阅读教学最佳方法的两大主流学派。

sentences.en: So, if you'll indulge us.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, probably the dominant way over the past few decades has been a school of thought called balanced literacy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，过去几十年里占主导地位的教学法被称为“平衡识字法”。

sentences.en: And balanced literacy really focuses on letting children choose those books that they gravitate toward, giving them a lot of time to read quietly by themselves,
sentences.zh: 平衡识字法真正关注的是让孩子们选择他们感兴趣的书籍，给他们充足的时间安静地阅读，

sentences.en: having children sort of really focus on the meaning of stories, what happens in them, and really look a lot at the pictures, even use the pictures to guess the words on the page.
sentences.zh: 让孩子们专注于故事的含义、情节的发展，并大量观察图片，甚至利用图片来猜测书页上的单词。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Let's demonstrate balanced literacy through this delightful-looking book in front of us.
sentences.zh: 让我们通过眼前这本看起来很可爱的书来演示一下平衡识字法。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: This is a book called Mixing Colors, My Five-Year-Old Daughter Brought It Home From Her Classroom, which has a balanced literacy library in it.
sentences.zh: 这本书叫《混合颜色》，是我五岁的女儿从学校带回来的，她的学校里就有平衡识字法的图书馆。

sentences.en: And let's go ahead and open the book.
sentences.zh: 我们把书打开看看。

sentences.en: It has a big splotch of red paint, a big splotch of yellow paint, and then it shows them mixing together to form orange.
sentences.zh: 书里有一大块红色颜料，一大块黄色颜料，然后展示了它们混合在一起变成了橙色。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If I can read it, it says, red and yellow make orange.
sentences.zh: 如果我来读的话，上面写着：红色和黄色混合成橙色。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there's a few things I would just call your attention to about this page.
sentences.zh: 关于这一页，我想请你注意几点。

sentences.en: First of all, you can kind of guess what the words will be by the colors, right?
sentences.zh: 首先，你可以通过颜色猜出单词是什么，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, five-year-olds, six-year-olds in kindergarten, they know their colors already, and so they very little even need to look at the words to get what they said.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，五六岁的幼儿园孩子已经认识颜色了，所以他们几乎不需要看单词就能知道上面写了什么。

sentences.en: I think my two-year-old son would say red, yellow.
sentences.zh: 我想我两岁的儿子也会说红色、黄色。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The other thing I would point out is while the concepts of the colors are very easy, the words themselves are really hard for a kindergartner.
sentences.zh: 我要指出的另一点是，虽然颜色的概念很简单，但对于幼儿园的孩子来说，这些单词本身其实很难。

sentences.en: Yellow is a really hard word.
sentences.zh: “Yellow”（黄色）是一个很难的词。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: It has some irregular pronunciations, and so is orange.
sentences.zh: 它的发音有些不规则，“Orange”（橙色）也是如此。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The second method.
sentences.zh: 第二种方法。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This book is part of a set that's based on something called The Science of Reading, and it heavily focuses on phonics.
sentences.zh: 这本书属于一套基于“阅读科学”的教材，它非常强调自然拼读法（phonics）。

sentences.en: The Science of Reading and phonics are ways that teach children to read through a really sequenced introduction to the sounds and letter combinations that make up the English language.
sentences.zh: 阅读科学和自然拼读法是通过对英语语言中的发音和字母组合进行系统化的介绍来教孩子阅读的方法。

sentences.en: So we wouldn't be introducing the word yellow, for example, before we do cat, dog, and other very simple words like that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们不会在教“cat”（猫）、“dog”（狗）这类非常简单的词之前，就引入“yellow”这样的词。

sentences.en: That teach us what those consonants and vowels do.
sentences.zh: 这些简单的词能教我们辅音和元音的作用。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So we're opening up this book.
sentences.zh: 我们打开这本书。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The book is called Sam, and the purpose of this book, as we'll notice, is really to teach that the letter A in many cases says ah.
sentences.zh: 这本书叫《萨姆》（Sam），正如我们将注意到的，这本书的目的是为了教授字母A在许多情况下发“ah”的音。

sentences.en: So page one says Sam and cat.
sentences.zh: 所以第一页写着“Sam and cat”（萨姆和猫）。

sentences.en: So it has three different uses of A saying ah in three different words.
sentences.zh: 它在三个不同的单词中使用了三次字母A发“ah”音的情况。

sentences.en: Sam and cat.
sentences.zh: 萨姆和猫。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And let's just do one more page.
sentences.zh: 我们再看一页。

sentences.en: Matt and cat.
sentences.zh: 马特和猫。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And there's no way I would know that that fellow is Matt because he's not a splotch of red paint.
sentences.zh: 而且我根本不可能知道那个家伙是马特，因为他不是一块红色的颜料。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You would not know that his name was Matt if you didn't read the book.
sentences.zh: 如果你不读这本书，你根本不知道他的名字叫马特。

sentences.en: Okay, so to summarize, balanced literacy focuses more on stories, context, illustrations.
sentences.zh: 好的，总结一下，平衡识字法更侧重于故事、语境和插图。

sentences.en: It's learning to read a word by considering the meaning of the story and what word might fit into the themes and the images on the page.
sentences.zh: 它是通过考虑故事的含义以及什么词可能符合书页上的主题和图像来学习阅读单词。

sentences.en: By contrast, science of reading includes a big dose of phonics, which is to say a kid learns the letters sounds, the consonants, vowels,
sentences.zh: 相比之下，阅读科学包含了大量的自然拼读法，也就是说，孩子要学习字母的发音、辅音、元音，

sentences.en: the common combinations that we talked about like ca for cat, and therefore is going to sound out the words rather than try to rely on contextual clues.
sentences.zh: 以及我们刚才提到的像“ca”代表“cat”这样的常见组合，因此孩子会拼读单词，而不是试图依赖语境线索。

sentences.en: You got it.
sentences.zh: 你说对了。

sentences.en: And the two schools of thought represented by these two books, balanced literacy on one hand and the science of reading on the other,
sentences.zh: 而这两本书所代表的两种思想流派，一边是平衡识字法，另一边是阅读科学，

sentences.en: have been battling it out in this country for decades as to which is the best method, the right method for teaching young children how to read.
sentences.zh: 几十年来一直在美国争论不休，争论哪种才是教幼儿阅读的最佳方法、正确方法。

sentences.en: And reading, of course, is the most fundamental skill of all schooling.
sentences.zh: 当然，阅读是所有学校教育中最基础的技能。

sentences.en: Reading is the first thing kids need to do when they get to school.
sentences.zh: 阅读是孩子们上学后首先需要做的事情。

sentences.en: And what's happening right now is a big and important reckoning over which of these methods is right and which is wrong.
sentences.zh: 而现在正在发生的是一场关于哪种方法正确、哪种方法错误的重大且重要的清算。

sentences.en: And how did we get to this overdue moment of reckoning?
sentences.zh: 我们是如何走到这一迟来的清算时刻的？

sentences.en: Let's start in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 让我们从20世纪60年代说起。

sentences.en: At that time, there was really no settled way to teach children how to read.
sentences.zh: 那时，教孩子阅读并没有统一的方法。

sentences.en: But in the late 1960s, early 1970s, something was happening in education and the counterculture.
sentences.zh: 但在60年代末、70年代初，教育界和反主流文化运动中发生了一些变化。

sentences.en: And it was this idea that all learning should be based on the child's curiosity, that children could sort of naturally figure it out on their own if given the right environment.
sentences.zh: 当时有一种观点认为，所有的学习都应该基于孩子的好奇心，如果环境合适，孩子们可以自然而然地自己弄明白。

sentences.en: And one person in particular really embodies that school of thought and came to be a real leader in the United States with this idea.
sentences.zh: 有一个人特别体现了这种思想流派，并凭借这一理念成为了美国真正的领军人物。

sentences.en: And her name is Lucy Calkins.
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫露西·卡尔金斯。

sentences.en: And what should we know about Lucy Calkins?
sentences.zh: 关于露西·卡尔金斯，我们应该了解些什么？

sentences.en: Lucy Calkins grew up outside Buffalo.
sentences.zh: 露西·卡尔金斯在布法罗郊外长大。

sentences.en: She was one of nine children.
sentences.zh: 她是九个孩子中的一个。

sentences.en: And although her parents were doctors, they also maintained a working farm.
sentences.zh: 虽然她的父母都是医生，但他们也经营着一个农场。

sentences.en: And they put the kids to work on the farm.
sentences.zh: 他们让孩子们在农场干活。

sentences.en: So it's a bit of an eccentric family.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个有点古怪的家庭。

sentences.en: Or idyllic, depending on your view.
sentences.zh: 或者说是田园诗般的，取决于你的看法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: She said she worked really hard.
sentences.zh: 她说她工作非常努力。

sentences.en: And she learned how much a child can really do because her and her siblings were expected to care for these animals.
sentences.zh: 她了解到一个孩子能做的事情有多少，因为她和兄弟姐妹们被要求照顾这些动物。

sentences.en: And she always was really interested in teaching.
sentences.zh: 而且她一直对教学非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: So do you mind if I ask you some biographical questions?
sentences.zh: 你不介意我问你一些个人背景问题吧？

sentences.en: No, just go ahead.
sentences.zh: 没关系，尽管问。

sentences.en: I'm all set to do whatever you want.
sentences.zh: 我已经准备好回答你想问的任何问题了。

sentences.en: I know you got started.
sentences.zh: 我知道你是怎么开始的。

sentences.en: And over the course of my reporting,
sentences.zh: 在我的报道过程中，

sentences.en: I had the opportunity to interview Professor Calkins and speak to her about how she got started in teaching and how she came to develop her ideas about how children learn.
sentences.zh: 我有机会采访了卡尔金斯教授，并与她谈论了她是如何开始教书的，以及她是如何发展出关于儿童学习方式的理念的。

sentences.en: I wanted to be a good teacher.
sentences.zh: 我想成为一名好老师。

sentences.en: I taught with fervor.
sentences.zh: 我满怀热情地教学。

sentences.en: But I didn't know what I was doing.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: And I needed to know more.
sentences.zh: 我需要了解更多。

sentences.en: And in the early 1970s, she decided to go apprentice herself in the elementary schools in England.
sentences.zh: 20世纪70年代初，她决定去英国的小学当学徒。

sentences.en: And the reason she wanted to do that is because they were known as being at the forefront at that time of progressive, child-centered education.
sentences.zh: 她之所以想这样做，是因为当时英国小学被认为是进步的、以儿童为中心的教育的前沿。

sentences.en: The idea that children's curiosity could really drive learning, that teachers were guides to develop kids' curiosity,
sentences.zh: 这种理念认为孩子的好奇心可以真正驱动学习，老师是培养孩子好奇心的向导，

sentences.en: not that teachers had all the answers or the adult was the real leader of the classroom.
sentences.zh: 而不是老师掌握所有答案，或者成年人是课堂的绝对领导者。

sentences.en: So the opposite of the teacher with the stick at the front saying, like, look at the chalkboard and this is what we're doing.
sentences.zh: 所以这与那种拿着教鞭站在前面说“看黑板，我们要学这个”的老师截然相反。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what Lucy Calkins wanted to get away from.
sentences.zh: 而这正是露西·卡尔金斯想要摆脱的。

sentences.en: So I flew to Heathrow and hitchhiked, stuck out my thumb and hitchhiked to Oxfordshire.
sentences.zh: 所以我飞到希思罗机场，然后搭便车，伸出大拇指搭车去了牛津郡。

sentences.en: So she goes over to the U.K.
sentences.zh: 所以她去了英国，

sentences.en: and she's in Oxfordshire.
sentences.zh: 待在牛津郡。

sentences.en: And she absolutely falls in love with the type of teaching that she sees in those elementary schools.
sentences.zh: 她彻底爱上了她在那些小学里看到的教学方式。

sentences.en: So the teaching was a kind of a simple, highly structured kind of really workshop so that the teacher could be responsive.
sentences.zh: 那种教学是一种简单、高度结构化的工作坊形式，以便老师能够做出及时的反馈。

sentences.en: Kids were deeply engaged in projects.
sentences.zh: 孩子们深度参与到项目中。

sentences.en: There was an emphasis on craftsmanship and care.
sentences.zh: 强调工艺和细心。

sentences.en: Like, for example, she told me about watching children just arrayed in front of a mushroom.
sentences.zh: 例如，她告诉我她看到孩子们排成一排观察蘑菇。

sentences.en: You know, they would have the kids very painstakingly observe the mushroom and try to draw it with great accuracy and, you know, careful, invested, deep work.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们会让孩子们非常费心地观察蘑菇，并试图极其准确地画出来，这是一种细致、投入、深入的工作。

sentences.en: And they spend an hour just looking at the different parts of the mushroom and sketching it in their notebooks and coloring it in.
sentences.zh: 他们花了一个小时只是观察蘑菇的不同部分，在笔记本上素描，并涂上颜色。

sentences.en: This is very 60s, 70s.
sentences.zh: 这非常有60、70年代的风格。

sentences.en: Yes, that's very creative.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常有创意。

sentences.en: And I think there's definitely a strong appeal to this.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这绝对有很强的吸引力。

sentences.en: You know, I think about, say, taking my five-year-old to the park and she might say, look at this flower.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想起带我五岁的女儿去公园，她可能会说，看这朵花。

sentences.en: And we can talk about how the sun and the rain help it to grow and notice how many puddles it has, its color.
sentences.zh: 我们可以谈谈阳光和雨水是如何帮助它生长的，注意它有多少花瓣，它的颜色。

sentences.en: So, of course, children's curiosity does drive a lot of their learning.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，孩子的好奇心确实驱动了他们大部分的学习。

sentences.en: And there is an intuitive truth here.
sentences.zh: 这里面确实有一种直觉上的真理。

sentences.en: So what emerges from this experience that Lucy Calkin has in the U.K.?
sentences.zh: 那么，露西·卡尔金斯在英国的这段经历产生了什么结果？

sentences.en: Well, what eventually comes out of this is a strong philosophy that she has, a theory, that children can use these curiosity, inquiry-based methods to learn anything,
sentences.zh: 最终产生的是她的一种强有力的哲学，一种理论，即孩子们可以利用这些基于好奇心和探究的方法来学习任何东西，

sentences.en: including how to read.
sentences.zh: 包括如何阅读。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So how does she proceed down this path?
sentences.zh: 那么她是如何走上这条道路的？

sentences.en: Interestingly, she gets her Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，她获得了博士学位，

sentences.en: in teaching children how to write, not how to read.
sentences.zh: 研究的是教孩子写作，而不是阅读。

sentences.en: And she does something in writing education that is really revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 她在写作教育方面做了一些真正革命性的事情。

sentences.en: You know, prior to the work of Lucy Calkin's and colleagues of hers, a lot of teaching children how to write was really rote.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在露西·卡尔金斯和她的同事们的工作之前，很多教孩子写作的方法真的很死板。

sentences.en: It was boring.
sentences.zh: 很无聊。

sentences.en: It was about spelling, grammar, penmanship.
sentences.zh: 内容全是拼写、语法、书法。

sentences.en: And while those things are important, they might not have really sparked kids' desire to write all that much.
sentences.zh: 虽然这些东西很重要，但它们可能并没有真正激发孩子们写作的欲望。

sentences.en: And what Lucy Calkin's did is she took the concept of sort of a graduate school writing workshop for adult writers where you keep a journal, you practice writing about your life.
sentences.zh: 而露西·卡尔金斯所做的是，她借鉴了成人写作工作坊的概念，即写日记，练习写关于自己生活的内容。

sentences.en: And she said, let's have elementary school writers do this.
sentences.zh: 她说，让我们让小学生也这样做。

sentences.en: And what was really interesting about this is that when elementary school kids were given writers' notebooks and journals and they were encouraged to write without focusing too much on stuff like spelling,
sentences.zh: 真正有趣的是，当小学生们拿到写作笔记本和日记本，并被鼓励在不纠结于拼写等细节的情况下写作时，

sentences.en: many of them really could do it.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人真的能做到。

sentences.en: So this worked.
sentences.zh: 所以这奏效了。

sentences.en: Yeah, for many kids, not for all, but for many kids, it did work really well.
sentences.zh: 是的，对很多孩子来说，虽然不是全部，但对很多孩子而言，这确实非常有效。

sentences.en: And teachers absolutely loved this.
sentences.zh: 而且老师们非常喜欢这一点。

sentences.en: So Lucy Calkin's, you know, through the 80s and 90s, she became so beloved for her writing workshop technique for young children.
sentences.zh: 所以露西·卡尔金斯（Lucy Calkins），你知道，在整个80年代和90年代，她因为针对幼儿的写作工作坊教学法而备受推崇。

sentences.en: But she starts to hear more and more from teachers, and she notices herself when she's going across the country training educators that for kids who struggle with writing,
sentences.zh: 但她开始越来越多地听到老师们的反馈，而且当她去全国各地培训教育工作者时，她自己也注意到，对于那些在写作上有困难的孩子来说，

sentences.en: reading is really at the core.
sentences.zh: 阅读才是真正的核心。

sentences.en: That reading is the fundamental skill that they need to get down if they're going to become great, enthusiastic writers.
sentences.zh: 阅读是他们想要成为优秀、热情的作家所必须掌握的基本技能。

sentences.en: So she decides that she wants to start exploring, creating her own approach to reading, something that would draw upon what she sees as the strengths of what she did with writing,
sentences.zh: 于是她决定开始探索，创造自己的一套阅读教学方法，这种方法要汲取她认为自己在写作教学中所做出的优势，

sentences.en: something that centers the child, lets their curiosity guide the curriculum, and gives the student a lot of free choice in what they read.
sentences.zh: 即以孩子为中心，让他们的好奇心引导课程，并给学生在阅读内容上有很大的自由选择权。

sentences.en: And so at that point in the late 1990s and early 2000s, she begins to branch out into the teaching of reading.
sentences.zh: 因此，在20世纪90年代末和21世纪初，她开始涉足阅读教学领域。

sentences.en: So what happens when she brings this approach to reading?
sentences.zh: 那么，当她把这种方法引入阅读教学时，发生了什么呢？

sentences.en: So she comes out with a book in the early 2000s called The Art of Teaching Reading.
sentences.zh: 她在21世纪初出版了一本名为《阅读教学的艺术》（The Art of Teaching Reading）的书。

sentences.en: And it very much calls back to her earlier work on The Art of Teaching Writing.
sentences.zh: 这本书在很大程度上呼应了她早期的著作《写作教学的艺术》（The Art of Teaching Writing）。

sentences.en: She takes a workshop approach.
sentences.zh: 她采用了工作坊式的教学方法。

sentences.en: She gives children a lot of free time in the classroom to sort of pick books and quietly read.
sentences.zh: 她在课堂上给孩子们留出大量的自由时间，让他们去挑选书籍并安静地阅读。

sentences.en: She starts doing this in kindergarten.
sentences.zh: 她从幼儿园开始这样做。

sentences.en: Kindergarten students, for the most part, cannot read.
sentences.zh: 幼儿园的学生，大多数情况下，是不会阅读的。

sentences.en: So what they're doing quietly when they are, quote-unquote, reading is really just flipping the pages and kind of looking at the pictures and the words, not actually reading.
sentences.zh: 所以当他们“所谓”在安静阅读时，其实只是在翻书，看着图片和文字，并不是真的在阅读。

sentences.en: And she has a real approach to sounding out words or phonics.
sentences.zh: 而且她对拼读单词或自然拼读法有一套自己的看法。

sentences.en: She's skeptical of it.
sentences.zh: 她对此持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: She acknowledges that phonics is part of learning to read.
sentences.zh: 她承认自然拼读是学习阅读的一部分。

sentences.en: But rather than sort of spend a lot of classroom time teaching children the correspondence between the letters on the page and the sounds we hear in spoken language,
sentences.zh: 但她并不主张花大量课堂时间去教孩子们页面上的字母与我们口语中听到的声音之间的对应关系，

sentences.en: she cautions that doing this in too structured of a way is really going to turn kids off.
sentences.zh: 她告诫说，以过于结构化的方式进行教学反而会引起孩子们的反感。

sentences.en: And she even says, if a kid is struggling to correctly read the word, don't have them sound out the letters.
sentences.zh: 她甚至说，如果孩子在正确阅读单词时遇到困难，不要让他们去拼读字母。

sentences.en: That's not how you should prompt them.
sentences.zh: 那不是你应该引导他们的方式。

sentences.en: Instead, you should have them flip back through the pages of the book, consider the meaning of the story, look at the pictures, and think about what word could be right.
sentences.zh: 相反，你应该让他们翻回书页，考虑故事的含义，观察图片，并思考哪个词可能是对的。

sentences.en: Really interesting.
sentences.zh: 真有意思。

sentences.en: So this approach is fundamentally not about phonics, maybe even a little anti-phonics.
sentences.zh: 所以这种方法从根本上来说不是关于自然拼读的，甚至可能还有点反自然拼读。

sentences.en: She might resist that if you said it that way because what she'll say is, I always said there was some place for it.
sentences.zh: 如果你这样说，她可能会反驳，因为她会说，我一直都说它有其存在的空间。

sentences.en: But that's really not what teachers took from her writing and from the speeches she gave.
sentences.zh: 但那确实不是老师们从她的著作和演讲中领会到的内容。

sentences.en: They took from her writing and the speeches she gave that focusing too much on phonics is going to harm children.
sentences.zh: 他们从她的著作和演讲中领会到的是，过分关注自然拼读会伤害孩子。

sentences.en: They should be thinking about the meaning of stories.
sentences.zh: 他们应该思考故事的含义。

sentences.en: They should be enjoying the pictures on the page.
sentences.zh: 他们应该享受书页上的图片。

sentences.en: When they struggle, they should guess.
sentences.zh: 当他们遇到困难时，他们应该去猜。

sentences.en: Guess what the word is based on the meaning of the story and the pictures that they see.
sentences.zh: 根据故事的含义和他们看到的图片来猜这个词是什么。

sentences.en: Don't labor over the letters in the word.
sentences.zh: 不要在单词的字母上费劲。

sentences.en: Okay, so how influential does this approach that Lucy Calkins is, it sounds like pioneering, become?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么露西·卡尔金斯这种听起来像是开创性的方法，影响力有多大呢？

sentences.en: Very influential.
sentences.zh: 非常有影响力。

sentences.en: And as balanced literacy grows and Lucy Calkins' curriculum materials spread out across the country, there's a big upside for her.
sentences.zh: 随着平衡识字法（balanced literacy）的发展和露西·卡尔金斯的课程材料在全国范围内的传播，这对她来说是一个巨大的利好。

sentences.en: She's in business.
sentences.zh: 她做成了生意。

sentences.en: She is, and in addition to being a professor at Columbia University, she has two private companies, a domestic private company and a foreign one,
sentences.zh: 确实，除了担任哥伦比亚大学的教授外，她还拥有两家私营公司，一家国内私营公司和一家国外公司，

sentences.en: that sell these materials and sell teacher training across the United States and around the world.
sentences.zh: 在全美乃至全球销售这些材料并提供教师培训。

sentences.en: And by the early 2000s, it becomes the primary way that teachers and graduate schools of education are taught to teach children how to read,
sentences.zh: 到了21世纪初，这成为了教师和教育研究生院教授儿童阅读的主要方式，

sentences.en: and it becomes the way that probably about half or more of American elementary schools teach kids.
sentences.zh: 并且这成为了大约一半甚至更多美国小学教孩子阅读的方式。

sentences.en: And to give you an example of how much success she's having selling this curriculum,
sentences.zh: 为了让你了解她在销售这套课程方面取得了多大的成功，

sentences.en: New York City, the largest district in the country which educates one million children,
sentences.zh: 纽约市，这个全国最大的学区，教育着一百万名儿童，

sentences.en: in the early 2000s under Mayor Michael Bloomberg, actually mandated that schools use Lucy Calkins' methods and materials.
sentences.zh: 在21世纪初迈克尔·布隆伯格（Michael Bloomberg）市长任内，实际上强制要求学校使用露西·卡尔金斯的方法和材料。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So to call back to the beginning of our conversation, to the degree that there's been a big, long battle in this country over the right way to learn to read
sentences.zh: 所以回到我们谈话的开头，在某种程度上，这个国家关于学习阅读的正确方式一直存在着一场漫长的激烈争论，

sentences.en: between the science of reading, this phonics-based approach, and balanced literacy, this Lucy Calkins approach,
sentences.zh: 即阅读科学（基于自然拼读的方法）与平衡识字法（这种露西·卡尔金斯的方法）之间的争论，

sentences.en: it sounds like around this point, by the time New York City is adopting this in such a profound way,
sentences.zh: 听起来在这一点上，当纽约市如此深刻地采用这种方法时，

sentences.en: as are so many other districts, that Lucy Calkins' approach, balanced literacy, is winning.
sentences.zh: 正如其他许多学区一样，露西·卡尔金斯的方法，即平衡识字法，正在获胜。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely, that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样，确实如此。

sentences.en: But while she was pushing this out across the country and it was wielding so much influence and so many teachers and students were falling under its sway,
sentences.zh: 但当她在全国范围内推广这种方法，并且它发挥了如此大的影响力，以至于许多老师和学生都受到其影响时，

sentences.en: there was something else happening that was really casting doubt on whether this was truly the best way to teach children how to read.
sentences.zh: 还有另一件事正在发生，这让人真正怀疑这是否真的是教孩子阅读的最佳方式。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: 33 Presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 Super Sundays.
sentences.zh: 60个超级星期天。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟中最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world.
sentences.zh: 庆祝175年来帮助你了解世界。

sentences.en: And make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受特别优惠，网址是 nytimes.com/subscribe。

sentences.en: So Dana, tell us about this doubt that's starting to emerge about balanced literacy and Lucy Calkin's now very popular best-selling approach to how to read.
sentences.zh: 那么达娜（Dana），告诉我们关于这种开始出现的对平衡识字法以及露西·卡尔金斯现在非常流行、畅销的阅读教学方法的质疑。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, there were always voices in dissent to her approach and to the balanced literacy philosophy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一直都有反对她这种方法和平衡识字法理念的声音。

sentences.en: And a really important group of dissent were parents of children with dyslexia.
sentences.zh: 而一个非常重要的反对群体是阅读障碍儿童的家长。

sentences.en: They were saying, my kid is not learning how to read in school.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我的孩子在学校里学不会阅读。

sentences.en: I went out and I had to pay with my own money for really expensive tutoring.
sentences.zh: 我不得不自掏腰包去请非常昂贵的家教。

sentences.en: And guess what the tutor did with my child?
sentences.zh: 你猜家教对我的孩子做了什么？

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: Taught them phonics.
sentences.zh: 教他们自然拼读。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, my child, who was diagnosed with a learning disability and was really struggling, is at least able to get the basics down, is able to read.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，我那个被诊断出有学习障碍、一直非常挣扎的孩子，至少能够掌握基础知识，能够阅读了。

sentences.en: And why should I have to pay for this?
sentences.zh: 为什么我必须为此付费？

sentences.en: What about parents who can't afford to pay?
sentences.zh: 那些付不起钱的家长怎么办？

sentences.en: Schools, you have let us down.
sentences.zh: 学校，你们让我们失望了。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: But those parents were sort of seen as squeaky wheels, advocating for their particular children.
sentences.zh: 但这些家长被视为“爱叫的轮子”（指爱抱怨的人），在为他们自己的孩子争取权益。

sentences.en: And perhaps they were asking for something that wasn't right for the general group of learners.
sentences.zh: 也许他们要求的东西并不适合广大的学习者群体。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And I think school districts saw it as a niche request to a large degree.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为学区在很大程度上将其视为一种小众诉求。

sentences.en: So you're saying dissent and doubt a little bit gets disregarded and maybe kind of bulldozed.
sentences.zh: 所以你是说，异议和怀疑在一定程度上被忽视了，甚至可能被某种程度上强行压制了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Now, here's a really interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 现在，这里有一件非常有趣的事情。

sentences.en: Starting around the 1990s, functional magnetic resonance imaging, the MRI machine, allowed
sentences.zh: 从20世纪90年代左右开始，功能性磁共振成像（MRI）机器，允许

sentences.en: researchers to look at the brain of a reader, of children learning to read, of adult readers.
sentences.zh: 研究人员观察阅读者、正在学习阅读的儿童以及成年阅读者的大脑。

sentences.en: And it really shed a lot of light on how it is that reading takes place in the brain.
sentences.zh: 它确实揭示了大脑中阅读是如何发生的。

sentences.en: And what did it find?
sentences.zh: 它发现了什么？

sentences.en: It found that while we're reading, we're using a lot of those parts of our brain that we use for speaking and listening.
sentences.zh: 它发现我们在阅读时，使用了许多我们用于说话和听力的脑部区域。

sentences.en: And those parts are doing the hard work of connecting those letters and words on the page
sentences.zh: 而这些区域正在进行艰苦的工作，将页面上的字母和单词连接起来，

sentences.en: to what we all do naturally know how to do as human beings, which is to speak and to listen to language.
sentences.zh: 连接到我们作为人类天生就知道如何做的事情上，那就是说话和听语言。

sentences.en: And that's what reading is.
sentences.zh: 这就是阅读。

sentences.en: Reading is the work of connecting letters and words to the sounds of spoken language.
sentences.zh: 阅读是将字母和单词与口语声音连接起来的工作。

sentences.en: So that is an understanding of reading as being profoundly auditory.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种将阅读理解为深刻的听觉过程的观点。

sentences.en: And from what you've been describing of Lucy Calkin's work, she has deliberately de-emphasized that notion of sounding out words in a rigorous way.
sentences.zh: 根据你所描述的露西·卡尔金斯的工作，她刻意淡化了那种以严谨方式拼读单词的观念。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The MRI machine made a really helpful intervention here.
sentences.zh: 核磁共振成像机器在这里进行了一次非常有益的干预。

sentences.en: It gave us some really big clues that leaving out the sounded out piece, the phonics piece, was going to really do children a disservice.
sentences.zh: 它给了我们一些非常重要的线索，即忽略拼读部分，也就是自然拼读部分，真的会给孩子们带来伤害。

sentences.en: So by the time Lucy Calkin's reading curriculum is becoming ascendant and adopted in places like New York City, Dana, as you have told us, there's actually anecdotal evidence that
sentences.zh: 所以，当露西·卡尔金斯的阅读课程在纽约市等地变得盛行并被采用时，达娜，正如你告诉我们的，实际上有轶事证据表明

sentences.en: it's not working for key groups of kids like those with dyslexia.
sentences.zh: 它对像阅读障碍儿童这样的关键群体并不奏效。

sentences.en: And then this scientific evidence that the entire approach is basically kind of wrong based on how the human brain works and how we learn to read.
sentences.zh: 然后还有科学证据表明，基于人类大脑的工作方式以及我们学习阅读的方式，整个方法基本上是错误的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And what happens over the past, say, six or seven years is that the doubt grows and grows due to a few key developments.
sentences.zh: 而在过去六七年里发生的事情是，由于几个关键的发展，这种怀疑越来越强烈。

sentences.en: First of all, there's all of these test scores coming out that are showing that it's just so persistent that about a third of children in America do not have basic reading skills.
sentences.zh: 首先，所有的测试分数都显示，大约三分之一的美国儿童没有基本的阅读技能，这种情况非常顽固。

sentences.en: And from a civil rights perspective, although all children are affected by these reading problems, they cut across class, they cut across race, it is the fact that low-income
sentences.zh: 从民权的角度来看，虽然所有儿童都受到这些阅读问题的影响，它们跨越了阶级、跨越了种族，但事实是低收入

sentences.en: children are affected most by these probleMs.
sentences.zh: 儿童受这些问题的影响最大。

sentences.en: And so there's a real equity issue here too.
sentences.zh: 所以这里也存在一个真正的公平问题。

sentences.en: And so people are frustrated.
sentences.zh: 因此人们感到沮丧。

sentences.en: And so that draws more people to learn about the science of how kids learn to read and become familiar with this doubt that exists about balanced literacy.
sentences.zh: 这吸引了更多人去了解关于孩子如何学习阅读的科学，并开始熟悉这种关于平衡识字法的怀疑。

sentences.en: I think scientific research on reading has progressed enormously and has yielded findings that are absolutely rock solid.
sentences.zh: 我认为关于阅读的科学研究已经取得了巨大的进步，并得出了绝对坚实的发现。

sentences.en: And there's some really important writers and thinkers that start to speak out.
sentences.zh: 而且有一些非常重要的作家和思想家开始公开发表意见。

sentences.en: One of them is Mark Seidenberg.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是马克·赛登伯格（Mark Seidenberg）。

sentences.en: He publishes a book called Language at the Speed of Sight.
sentences.zh: 他出版了一本书，名为《语言的视觉速度》（Language at the Speed of Sight）。

sentences.en: And what this book does, he's a cognitive scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 这本书的作用是，他是一位认知科学家。

sentences.en: It tries to bring that cognitive science to educators.
sentences.zh: 它试图将认知科学带给教育工作者。

sentences.en: A child who's learning to read already knows something about spoken language quite a lot.
sentences.zh: 一个正在学习阅读的孩子已经对口语有了一定的了解，甚至了解很多。

sentences.en: And their immediate problem is to figure out how print relates to spoken language.
sentences.zh: 他们当下的问题是弄清楚印刷文字与口语之间的关系。

sentences.en: And he goes out and he really gets quite a lot of attention for this book.
sentences.zh: 他走出去，这本书确实引起了相当大的关注。

sentences.en: For a long time, no one really knew how children learn to read.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间以来，没有人真正知道孩子是如何学习阅读的。

sentences.en: It was more debates among people who had philosophies.
sentences.zh: 这更多是持有不同哲学观点的人之间的辩论。

sentences.en: And there's a crusading journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 还有一位充满激情的记者。

sentences.en: Her name is Emily Hanford.
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫艾米丽·汉福德（Emily Hanford）。

sentences.en: She's an audio journalist with American Public Media.
sentences.zh: 她是美国公共媒体（American Public Media）的一名音频记者。

sentences.en: She starts to publish a series of audio documentaries about kids with dyslexia, about how we learn to read.
sentences.zh: 她开始发布一系列关于阅读障碍儿童以及我们如何学习阅读的音频纪录片。

sentences.en: Schools think they're teaching kids to read.
sentences.zh: 学校认为他们在教孩子阅读。

sentences.en: Of course they do.
sentences.zh: 当然他们是这么认为的。

sentences.en: But it turns out there's a big body of scientific research about reading and how kids learn to do it.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，关于阅读以及孩子如何学习阅读，存在大量的科学研究。

sentences.en: This research shows there are important skills that all kids need to learn to become good readers.
sentences.zh: 这项研究表明，所有孩子都需要学习重要的技能才能成为优秀的阅读者。

sentences.en: And in lots of schools, they aren't being taught these skills.
sentences.zh: 而在许多学校里，他们并没有被教授这些技能。

sentences.en: And many, many people listen to this in the education world.
sentences.zh: 教育界有非常多的人听了这些内容。

sentences.en: Teachers are sort of emailing these podcasts to each other and saying, oh my gosh.
sentences.zh: 老师们互相转发这些播客，并说，天哪。

sentences.en: And this is a real emotional time for teachers who are for the first time, some of them after 20, 30 years in the classroom,
sentences.zh: 对于那些第一次接触到关于孩子如何学习阅读的认知科学的老师来说，这是一个非常感性的时刻，其中一些人已经在课堂上待了20年、30年了。

sentences.en: being exposed to cognitive science on how kids learn to read.
sentences.zh: 他们正在接触关于孩子如何学习阅读的认知科学。

sentences.en: And many teachers I've interviewed have described to me a sort of nagging sense that something was off,
sentences.zh: 许多我采访过的老师向我描述了一种挥之不去的预感，觉得有什么地方不对劲，

sentences.en: that they had used these balanced literacy methods the best way they knew how, that they had really enjoyed going to those summer training programs with Lucy Calkins.
sentences.zh: 他们尽其所能使用了这些平衡识字法，他们确实很喜欢参加露西·卡尔金斯的那些暑期培训项目。

sentences.en: They admired her.
sentences.zh: 他们钦佩她。

sentences.en: They loved reading her books.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢读她的书。

sentences.en: And for teachers who just had that feeling maybe that they weren't reaching all the kids that they wanted to reach,
sentences.zh: 而对于那些仅仅有这种感觉，觉得他们没有触及到所有他们想要触及的孩子的老师来说，

sentences.en: who tried their best for years to find out that all this time there was powerful persuasive evidence that other methods are more effective,
sentences.zh: 那些多年来尽最大努力去发现，原来一直以来都有强有力的、令人信服的证据表明其他方法更有效，

sentences.en: it was devastating, emotionally, psychologically devastating for many educators.
sentences.zh: 这对许多教育工作者来说，在情感和心理上都是毁灭性的打击。

sentences.en: What you're describing, Dana, sounds like a huge clash in the making.
sentences.zh: 达娜，你所描述的听起来正酝酿着一场巨大的冲突。

sentences.en: All these teachers and parents learning that the way they have been teaching or that their kids have been taught to read was wrong or off through this podcast
sentences.zh: 所有这些老师和家长通过这个播客了解到，他们一直以来的教学方式，或者他们孩子学习阅读的方式是错误的或有偏差的，

sentences.en: or through this cognitive psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 或者通过这位认知心理学家了解到这一点。

sentences.en: And yet, Lucy Calkins' curriculum is still being taught across the country.
sentences.zh: 然而，露西·卡尔金斯的课程仍在全国范围内教授。

sentences.en: So, at some point, that clash does arrive, and it must be kind of spectacular.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某个时刻，这种冲突终会到来，而且场面一定会相当壮观。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You note the problematic use of balanced literacy, and I have experienced that firsthand both as a mom and a legislator.
sentences.zh: 你指出了“平衡识字法”存在的问题，作为一名母亲和立法者，我对此深有体会。

sentences.en: Over the past five, six years, a major change has occurred.
sentences.zh: 在过去的五六年里，发生了一个重大的变化。

sentences.en: Having been an educator and having many of us on this conference committee, it is amazing how trends cycle through, and they're not always good trends.
sentences.zh: 作为一名教育工作者，并且我们委员会中许多人都有过这种经历，令人惊讶的是，趋势总是循环往复，而且并不总是好的趋势。

sentences.en: More and more policymakers were clued into this debate that was going on about the science of reading.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的决策者开始关注这场关于阅读科学的辩论。

sentences.en: So, today, I'm calling for a renewed focus on literacy and on the way we teach reading in the state of Ohio.
sentences.zh: 因此，今天我呼吁俄亥俄州重新关注识字教育以及我们教授阅读的方式。

sentences.en: And dozens of states started to pass laws actually requiring that structured phonics be taught in elementary schools.
sentences.zh: 几十个州开始通过法律，强制要求在小学教授结构化自然拼读法。

sentences.en: Y'all, we don't have a science-based reading curriculum in this school district.
sentences.zh: 各位，我们学区没有基于科学的阅读课程。

sentences.en: We don't teach children phonics.
sentences.zh: 我们不教孩子们自然拼读。

sentences.en: And dozens of school districts began to pull Lucy Culkin's curriculum out of classrooMs.
sentences.zh: 几十个学区开始将露西·卡尔金斯的课程从课堂中撤出。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: Did you read about the Mississippi miracle yesterday?
sentences.zh: 你昨天读到关于“密西西比奇迹”的消息了吗？

sentences.en: That Mississippi's reading scores have shot way up.
sentences.zh: 密西西比州的阅读成绩大幅提升了。

sentences.en: We see it in places like Mississippi, Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 我们在密西西比州、华盛顿特区等地都看到了这一点。

sentences.en: You know, as a representative of the NAACP, we look at this as a civil rights issue.
sentences.zh: 你知道，作为全国有色人种协进会（NAACP）的代表，我们将此视为一个民权问题。

sentences.en: Our kids have to be able to read, and it has to start with the state.
sentences.zh: 我们的孩子必须能够阅读，而这必须从州政府层面开始。

sentences.en: It's in the state constitution that kids are supposed to get an education in California.
sentences.zh: 加州宪法规定，孩子们有权在加州接受教育。

sentences.en: Oak in California, where the NAACP was crucial in asking that Lucy Culkin's curriculum not be used anymore.
sentences.zh: 在加州的奥克兰，NAACP在要求停止使用露西·卡尔金斯的课程方面发挥了关键作用。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: A real coalition of people, left-right, civil rights groups, educators, parents coming together to push for change.
sentences.zh: 一个由左翼、右翼、民权团体、教育工作者和家长组成的真正联盟，正在共同推动变革。

sentences.en: In New York City, more than half of our students are not on grade level.
sentences.zh: 在纽约市，超过一半的学生没有达到年级水平。

sentences.en: And in a sign of just how big the shift is,
sentences.zh: 而这标志着转变的规模有多大，

sentences.en: New York City, Lucy Culkin's hometown, the first big district to really embrace her approach.
sentences.zh: 纽约市是露西·卡尔金斯的家乡，也是第一个真正采纳她教学方法的大学区。

sentences.en: Phonics and phonemic awareness has been missing in far too many of our schools, and we're going to fix that.
sentences.zh: 自然拼读和音素意识在太多的学校里缺失了，我们要解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Has decided that her materials are no longer on the approved list of ways to teach kids to read in the country's largest school district.
sentences.zh: 该学区已决定，在全国最大的学区中，她的教材不再被列入教授孩子阅读的批准名单中。

sentences.en: A huge blow to her curriculum, and I have to imagine to her reputation.
sentences.zh: 这对她的课程是一个巨大的打击，我想对她的声誉也是如此。

sentences.en: Massive.
sentences.zh: 非常巨大。

sentences.en: And this puts a lot of pressure on Lucy Culkin's and the product which she is trying to sell, which is a reading curriculum that does not include much phonics.
sentences.zh: 这给露西·卡尔金斯及其试图销售的产品带来了巨大压力，该产品是一套几乎不包含自然拼读的阅读课程。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So what does she do?
sentences.zh: 那么她该怎么办？

sentences.en: After initially resisting and fighting back, a huge turn happened.
sentences.zh: 在最初的抵制和反击之后，发生了一个巨大的转折。

sentences.en: She starts to acknowledge that she hasn't done maybe quite as good of a job as she could in including the science of reading and phonics in her curriculum.
sentences.zh: 她开始承认，在将阅读科学和自然拼读纳入课程方面，她做得可能不够好。

sentences.en: And about one year ago, she made an even bigger change.
sentences.zh: 大约一年前，她做出了一个更大的改变。

sentences.en: She created a version of her curriculum, which for the first time included daily structured phonics lessons.
sentences.zh: 她创建了一个版本的课程，首次包含了每日结构化的自然拼读课程。

sentences.en: And that is now for sale across the country.
sentences.zh: 目前这套课程正在全国范围内销售。

sentences.en: So she recognizes that she has missed a pretty big boat here in the story of how American kids learn to read,
sentences.zh: 所以她意识到，在美国孩子学习阅读的故事中，她错过了一个非常重要的机会，

sentences.en: and she adjusts in a way that I imagine, given the philosophy that you've been describing here,
sentences.zh: 她做出了调整，考虑到你在这里描述的哲学，

sentences.en: given her background, that experience in England, might have been very humbling and difficult.
sentences.zh: 考虑到她的背景，以及在英国的经历，这可能是一个非常谦卑且困难的过程。

sentences.en: I think it was really, really painful for her.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对她来说真的非常非常痛苦。

sentences.en: And last year, I did get the opportunity to have a really long interview with her about her process and coming to terms with this.
sentences.zh: 去年，我有机会与她进行了一次非常深入的采访，谈论了她的心路历程以及如何接受这一切。

sentences.en: And probably the biggest question I had was, given there has been science suggesting that phonics is really important for children, the MRI research,
sentences.zh: 我最大的疑问在于，鉴于已有科学研究表明自然拼读对儿童非常重要，比如核磁共振（MRI）研究，

sentences.en: but even prior to that, dating back to the 1960s, how is it that it's only been in the last few years that she made this change?
sentences.zh: 甚至在此之前，追溯到20世纪60年代，为什么直到最近几年她才做出这种改变？

sentences.en: And what does she say?
sentences.zh: 她是怎么说的？

sentences.en: What I feel right now is that the last two or three years, what I've learned from the science of reading work has been transformational
sentences.zh: 我现在的感受是，过去两三年里，我从阅读科学工作中学习到的东西是变革性的，

sentences.en: and has really made me a far better educator.
sentences.zh: 它确实让我成为了一名更好的教育工作者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, it really wasn't all that satisfying of an answer.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这个答案并不是那么令人满意。

sentences.en: She told me that she had clued into this the last few years.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，她是最近几年才意识到这一点的。

sentences.en: Probably after Emily Hanford's first, you know, stuff.
sentences.zh: 可能是在艾米丽·汉福德（Emily Hanford）的第一篇报道之后，你知道的。

sentences.en: She mentioned the journalist Emily Hanford.
sentences.zh: 她提到了记者艾米丽·汉福德。

sentences.en: She mentioned Mark Seidenberg, the cognitive psychologist I spoke about.
sentences.zh: 她提到了我之前提到的认知心理学家马克·赛登伯格（Mark Seidenberg）。

sentences.en: In other words, she was coming across this really powerful research alongside so many members of the public who were encountering it for the first time.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，她是在与许多第一次接触到这些研究的公众成员一起，接触到了这些非常有力的研究。

sentences.en: That's a hard concept to swallow for a leading educator, perhaps one of the leading educators when it comes to reading.
sentences.zh: 对于一位领先的教育工作者，或许是阅读领域最顶尖的教育工作者之一来说，这是一个很难接受的概念。

sentences.en: And somebody who works at a major university somehow had blinders on and never heard of this science that said that phonics was essential and her system had fundamental flaws.
sentences.zh: 一个在大型大学工作的人，竟然戴着眼罩，从未听说过这些证明自然拼读至关重要且她的系统存在根本缺陷的科学。

sentences.en: Do you find that credible?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这可信吗？

sentences.en: So I really tried to drill down on this with her over the course of several interviews.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的在几次采访中试图与她深入探讨这个问题。

sentences.en: Before that, were there ever opportunities for someone like you to meet with someone who looks at reading from a neuroscience type of background?
sentences.zh: 在此之前，像你这样的人是否有机会与那些从神经科学背景看待阅读的人会面？

sentences.en: How often, if ever, did that happen?
sentences.zh: 这种情况发生过吗，如果有，频率如何？

sentences.en: And maybe it never happened.
sentences.zh: 也许从来没有发生过。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Well, you certainly can't say that there's not opportunities to do that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你当然不能说没有机会这样做。

sentences.en: One of the things that really came out in our conversation is that she was working very much in the realm of theory and philosophy and ideas about reading.
sentences.zh: 我们谈话中真正体现的一点是，她非常沉浸在关于阅读的理论、哲学和理念领域。

sentences.en: These romantic ideas about child-driven learning, the child's curiosity driving the classroom, the teacher being a guide as opposed to sort of the bearer of information.
sentences.zh: 这些关于儿童驱动学习的浪漫想法，即孩子的好奇心驱动课堂，教师是引导者而不是信息的传递者。

sentences.en: And this was an ideology that was very strong in the part of the academy, the part of the university world that she came from.
sentences.zh: 这是一种在她所出身的学术界和大学世界中非常强大的意识形态。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't think that I thought about an MRI machine as part of how you get to know a reader.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我不认为她曾把核磁共振成像仪视为了解读者方式的一部分。

sentences.en: And as she said to me, she didn't think of MRI machines as a crucial piece of evidence in how kids learn.
sentences.zh: 正如她对我所说，她并不认为核磁共振成像仪是了解孩子如何学习的关键证据。

sentences.en: She said those types of researchers did not spend time in classrooMs.
sentences.zh: 她说那些类型的研究人员从不花时间在课堂里。

sentences.en: That was something that created skepticism for her and many of her colleagues.
sentences.zh: 这让她和她的许多同事产生了怀疑。

sentences.en: Like, we spend time talking to teachers, watching kids in classrooMs.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们花时间与老师交谈，观察课堂上的孩子。

sentences.en: Those cognitive scientists never go to K-12 schools.
sentences.zh: 那些认知科学家从不去K-12学校。

sentences.en: They don't know what an elementary school is like.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道小学是什么样的。

sentences.en: There was a sort of resistance there to accepting that those experts had much to say about what schools do.
sentences.zh: 对于接受这些专家对学校工作有发言权这一点，存在一种抵触情绪。

sentences.en: All of that makes a certain sense, Dana.
sentences.zh: 这一切在某种程度上是有道理的，达娜。

sentences.en: But I'm mindful of what you said about Lucy Calkins, which is that she's selling a curriculum.
sentences.zh: 但我记住了你关于露西·卡尔金斯所说的话，那就是她在销售课程。

sentences.en: So isn't it possible as well that this is a person who resisted absorbing evidence that her curriculum was wrong because she made a lot of money selling that curriculum?
sentences.zh: 那么，有没有可能她是一个抵制吸收证据的人，因为她通过销售那些错误的课程赚了很多钱？

sentences.en: You know, I can't look into her soul and know what drove her.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我无法看透她的灵魂，不知道是什么驱动了她。

sentences.en: I think that we all know that when our economic interests align with something we believe in really deeply, it's going to be really, really hard to doubt that.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都知道，当我们的经济利益与我们深信不疑的东西一致时，怀疑它会变得非常非常困难。

sentences.en: Right, doubly hard.
sentences.zh: 没错，难上加难。

sentences.en: So difficult.
sentences.zh: 太难了。

sentences.en: And I think that's what happened here.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是这里发生的事情。

sentences.en: But where I will give her credit is that there are other leaders in the balanced literacy world who have not made the changes that she has made
sentences.zh: 但我会给她应有的肯定，因为平衡识字领域的其他领导者并没有做出她那样的改变，

sentences.en: and have not even acknowledged, even up till now, 2023, that anything was wrong.
sentences.zh: 甚至直到现在，2023年，他们都没有承认有任何问题。

sentences.en: How does Lucy Calkins, and I'm sure this came up in your conversation with her,
sentences.zh: 露西·卡尔金斯是如何看待这里的问责概念的？我相信这在你们的谈话中也提到了。

sentences.en: think about the concept of accountability here?
sentences.zh: 因为根据科学和研究，

sentences.en: Because according to the science and research,
sentences.zh: 她和与她共事的人已经把许多许多孩子带入了歧途。

sentences.en: she and those she worked with have led lots and lots of kids astray.
sentences.zh: 她是否因为引导这么多人接受一种我们现在认为已被某种程度上证伪的阅读教学形式而感到内疚？

sentences.en: Does she feel guilty for basically leading so many people to embrace a form of the teaching of reading that we now think has been somewhat discredited?
sentences.zh: 我在这方面逼问了她。

sentences.en: I pushed her on this.
sentences.zh: 我问了她这个问题。

sentences.en: I asked her about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一些批评者想要的是更像道歉的东西。

sentences.en: You know, some critics, they want something more like an apology.
sentences.zh: 一些老师曾对我说，全国需要对阅读问题进行某种清算或哀悼过程。

sentences.en: Some teachers have said to me there needs to be almost like a national reckoning or grieving process for reading issues in the country.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为那些支持“自然拼读优先”的人，如果能向他人学习会很明智。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that people who have supported Onyx first would be wise to learn from others.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们可以为不信任老师、不给孩子提供重要且引人入胜的项目、不创造充满活力的课堂而道歉。

sentences.en: And that, sure, they could apologize for, you know, not trusting teachers, not giving kids important, engaging projects to work on, not creating classrooms that are vital.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为我们每个人都在尽力而为。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think that we all of us do the best we can.
sentences.zh: 她反问了这个问题，她说，其实，我认为那些极力推崇“自然拼读”的人才欠一个道歉。

sentences.en: She turned the question around, and she said, actually, I think those who pushed Onyx so heavily owe an apology.
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 她说，我认为他们忽视了快乐的重要性，忽视了写作的重要性，他们欠一个道歉。

sentences.en: She said, I think they owe an apology for overlooking the importance of joy, overlooking the importance of writing.
sentences.zh: 有人在问他们是否会因为忽视写作而道歉吗，

sentences.en: Is there, you know, are people asking whether they're going to apologize for overlooking writing,
sentences.zh: 因为没有邀请孩子们将他们自己重要的知识和故事带入课堂而道歉吗？

sentences.en: for not inviting kids to bring their own important knowledge and stories to the classroom?
sentences.zh: 他们会因为没有建立在孩子们的优势之上而道歉吗？

sentences.en: Are they going to apologize for not building on kids' strengths?
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，我们所有人都不完美，我们都在尽我们最大的努力。

sentences.en: I think, you know, all of us are imperfect, and we do the very, very best we can.
sentences.zh: 希望我们愿意说，你知道，我需要继续倾听他人的意见。

sentences.en: And hopefully we're willing to say, you know, I need to keep listening to others.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，她某种程度上利用了她继续视为其方法优势的东西，

sentences.en: In other words, she sort of drew upon what she continues to see as the strength of her approach,
sentences.zh: 而不是真正承认有什么东西真的真的错了。

sentences.en: as opposed to, I think, you know, truly acknowledging that something was really, really wrong.
sentences.zh: 这听起来不像是一个承担了很多责任的人，也不像是有任何悔意，事实可能确实如此，她并没有悔意。

sentences.en: That's not sounding like someone taking a lot of accountability, or sounding at all regretful, which is maybe the case, that she's not.
sentences.zh: 她个人并没有真正提供许多家长和老师所期待的道歉。

sentences.en: She has not personally really offered the apology that many parents and teachers are looking for.
sentences.zh: 当我们决定制作这一集时，我确实再次联系了她的团队，询问她的想法自我们上次交谈以来是否有所改变。

sentences.en: And when we decided to do this episode, I did reach back out to her team to ask her if her thinking had changed since we last spoke.
sentences.zh: 他们说没有。

sentences.en: And they said, no.
sentences.zh: 他们让我参考她去年已经给我的采访。

sentences.en: They referred me back to the interview she already gave me last year.
sentences.zh: 但有一个重大变化是，这些新教材正在销售中。

sentences.en: But one big thing that has changed, though, is that these new materials are for sale.
sentences.zh: 她已经告诉那15%到20%使用她旧教材的美国学校，他们应该进行更新。

sentences.en: And she has told the 15 to 20 percent of American schools that are using her old materials that they should update.
sentences.zh: 如果他们想购买新教材，可以获得折扣。

sentences.en: And if they want to buy the new stuff, they can get a discount.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管人们可能期待她有更感性的回应，

sentences.en: So even though folks may be looking to her for more of an emotive response,
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，看到她不再销售旧方法这一事实，对她网络内的学校来说将会有积极的改变。

sentences.en: I do think there will be positive change for schools in her network by seeing the fact that she is no longer selling the old approach.
sentences.zh: 达娜，从你所说的来看，这里发生的一切的结果，我们所经历的这段旅程最终到达了终点，

sentences.en: From what you're saying, Dana, the result of everything that's happened here, this journey that we've been on that's ended where it's ended,
sentences.zh: 那就是全国几十个，甚至几百个学区现在正在改变他们教授孩子阅读的方式。

sentences.en: is that dozens, maybe hundreds of school districts across the country are now changing how they teach kids to read.
sentences.zh: 我不得不想象这是一个非常混乱的过程，因为你谈论的是已经到位的课程，

sentences.en: And I have to imagine that's a pretty messy process because you're talking about curriculum that are in place,
sentences.zh: 老师们已经学会了如何使用这些课程，我不认为这就像按一下开关那么简单。

sentences.en: that teachers have been taught how to use, and I don't suspect that's like flipping a switch.
sentences.zh: 这真的很难。

sentences.en: It's really hard.
sentences.zh: 这非常昂贵。

sentences.en: It's really expensive.
sentences.zh: 你不仅要更换课程教材和课堂图书馆里的书籍，

sentences.en: You don't just have to replace the curriculum materials and the books in the classroom libraries.
sentences.zh: 你还必须对系统中的成年人进行再培训，其中一些人仍然相信这种旧方法。

sentences.en: You have to retrain the adults in the system, some of whom still believe in this.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常困难的转变。

sentences.en: So it's a very difficult shift.
sentences.zh: 那么进展如何？在我们所在的纽约市，这个全国最大的学区，情况是什么样的？

sentences.en: So how's it going, and what does it look like in a district like the one we're in, New York City, the biggest school district in the country?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我对此有一些个人经验。

sentences.en: Well, I have some personal experience with this.
sentences.zh: 我的女儿正在纽约市布鲁克林的公立学校完成她的幼儿园学年。

sentences.en: My daughter is finishing up her kindergarten year here in New York City Public Schools in Brooklyn.
sentences.zh: 在这个学年开始时，她带回家的这些书对她来说真的很难读，因为它们没有按顺序排列的自然拼读词汇。

sentences.en: And at the beginning of this school year, she brought home these books that are really hard for her to read because they don't have sequenced phonics words.
sentences.zh: 它们更偏向于平衡识字法。

sentences.en: They're more of a balanced literacy.
sentences.zh: 是的，那些平衡识字法的图书馆书籍，就像我们一开始看的《混合颜色》那本。

sentences.en: Yeah, the balanced literacy library books, like Mixing Colors, the one we started out looking at.
sentences.zh: 和她一起读这些书令人沮丧。

sentences.en: And it was frustrating to try to read the books with her.
sentences.zh: 她的老师要求我们在家里看这些书，但她真的很吃力。

sentences.en: Her teacher had asked us to look at them at home, but she was really struggling.
sentences.zh: 她在拼读那些单词时遇到了困难，因为它们对她来说有点难。

sentences.en: She was having trouble sounding out those words because they were a little bit hard for her.
sentences.zh: 但我得说，大约在学年中期，我注意到了一个巨大的转变。

sentences.en: But I will say, about halfway through the year, I noticed a huge shift.
sentences.zh: 我女儿的校长对这些变化充满热情，她一直要求老师们重新考虑他们在课堂上的做法。

sentences.en: My daughter's principal is enthusiastic about these changes, and she has been asking teachers to reconsider what they're doing in the classroom.
sentences.zh: 大约在学年中期，我的女儿塔莉亚开始告诉我，

sentences.en: And about halfway through the year, my daughter Talia started telling me,
sentences.zh: C-H发ch的音，S-H发sh的音。

sentences.en: C-H goes ch, S-H goes ch.
sentences.zh: 就在过去几周，她开始告诉我当E和I在一起，或者O和U在一起时会发生什么。

sentences.en: And just in the past few weeks, she started telling me about what happens when E and I are next to each other or O and U.
sentences.zh: 所以她绝对喜欢这个，我注意到她在拼读单词的能力上有巨大的变化。

sentences.en: And so she has absolutely loved this, and I've noticed a huge change in her ability to sound out the words.
sentences.zh: 她正在学习自然拼读，从你所说的来看，她现在因此成为了一名更好的读者。

sentences.en: She's being taught phonics, and it sounds, from what you're saying, like she's now a better reader as a result.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 她取得了巨大的进步。

sentences.en: She has made huge strides.
sentences.zh: 我必须问你一个复杂的问题。

sentences.en: I have to ask you a complicated question.
sentences.zh: 你是纽约市公立学校系统里一个孩子的家长，听起来，

sentences.en: You're a parent of a kid in the New York City public school system who, it sounds like,
sentences.zh: 你的孩子有一段时间一直在学习一些现在看来并不真正奏效的东西。

sentences.en: was being taught some of the stuff that now feels like it wasn't really working for a little bit of time.
sentences.zh: 你对此有什么感受？

sentences.en: I don't know how long.
sentences.zh: 我不知道要多久。

sentences.en: Do you find yourself mad at Lucy Calkins at all?
sentences.zh: 你对自己会因为露西·考尔金斯（Lucy Calkins）而感到生气吗？

sentences.en: You're not just a journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 你不仅仅是一名记者。

sentences.en: In this case, you're a parent.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，你是一位家长。

sentences.en: You're a New York City public school system parent.
sentences.zh: 你是纽约市公立学校系统的家长。

sentences.en: How do you think about that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么看待这件事的？

sentences.en: You know, that's a hard one.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很难说。

sentences.en: As a reporter, I try to stay above the fray and be objective.
sentences.zh: 作为一名记者，我尽量置身事外，保持客观。

sentences.en: Of course, as a parent, I'm not.
sentences.zh: 当然，作为家长，我做不到。

sentences.en: When I'm struggling with my kid to, you know, teach her not to look at the pictures,
sentences.zh: 当我努力教孩子不要只看图片，

sentences.en: but to look at the words when she's learning how to read, I have to admit, you know, I feel very frustrated.
sentences.zh: 而是在学习阅读时要看文字，我必须承认，你知道，我感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: But at the same time, there were some things Lucy Calkins was right about.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，露西·考尔金斯确实有些观点是正确的。

sentences.en: Phonics alone is not enough.
sentences.zh: 仅靠自然拼读法是不够的。

sentences.en: Kids do need access to books.
sentences.zh: 孩子们确实需要接触书籍。

sentences.en: They need a big vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 他们需要丰富的词汇量。

sentences.en: Writing is really important.
sentences.zh: 写作非常重要。

sentences.en: And, you know, for so many things in raising children, we do want to be guided by their curiosity.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在抚养孩子的许多事情上，我们确实希望以他们的好奇心为导向。

sentences.en: It's just that learning to read, really learning to read, is hard.
sentences.zh: 只是学习阅读，真正学会阅读，是一件难事。

sentences.en: And it is not natural.
sentences.zh: 而且这并非天生就会的。

sentences.en: Children cannot teach this to themselves.
sentences.zh: 孩子们无法自学成才。

sentences.en: Phonics is the crucial building block.
sentences.zh: 自然拼读法是至关重要的基石。

sentences.en: And Professor Calkins undersold it.
sentences.zh: 而考尔金斯教授低估了它的作用。

sentences.en: Well, Dana.
sentences.zh: 好的，达娜。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。
